summary.intent: Get an overall picture of where the Caliper project stands before alpha (full weekly measurement), then understand why the advertised 15x speed edge disappeared and find ways to cut cold-start cost, especially by avoiding the JSON boundary to the tsrs checker.
summary.outcome: Ran the full weekly (4 of 5 corpora measured; Chakra oracle timed out at 3600s), established that the 15x-39x claim was for structural-only mode while the default checker+dependencies mode is 1.3-3.3x cold and 5-24x on rerun, and found a real structural regression (Chakra 40->140ms). Spawned workers for a direct-call spike, request profiling, lazy HTML attributes, a no-JSON-text prototype and request reduction; the last two are still running, with a handoff briefing written for a separate session.

repo: The 15x-39x speed claim in docs/STATUS.md and docs/performance.md is for the structural resolver alone (--no-checker, no dependencies, 34-81 ms vs RDT 1.0-1.9 s, measured 2026-10-22); the default since 2026-11-12 is checker plus dependencies, which is much slower but gives the quality results.
Quality mode cold run is about 1.3-3.3x faster than RDT; a rerun over unchanged files is 5-24x faster than RDT's cold run because the checker's kept answer is reused.

The checker is the tsrs crates (upstream oxc-project/tsrs, pinned =0.24.0), called in process via tsrs_api::Session. Requests and answers are JSON text even in-process (ADR 0026 chose Session without comparing against direct tsrs_checker calls).

Cold shadcn profile: JSON codec ~21% of busy CPU, allocation/copying ~25%, tsrs checking only ~14.5%; about 32k requests for 1,802 components (~18 each). DOM/ES libs are bundled in the tsrs binary so lib caching would not help.
getSemanticDiagnostics on the generic-instantiation probe file (instantiate.rs:182) is one call costing ~580-800 ms, about 45% of handler time on shadcn.

Request profile: Chakra's batches contain 743k isReadonlySymbol sub-requests from Converter::fields; roughly 28k of 58.9k Chakra requests are identical repeats (getBaseTypes repeats 70-81%), which the converter's type-id memo does not catch; getPropertiesOfType returns ~113 KB per call (193 MB on shadcn).

ADR 0028: htmlAttributes `full` is the default so any attribute a body uses can become a typed row; it builds ~285 attribute types per component then relevance discards most (structural Chakra: full 170 ms, curated 90, none 40). Plan is lazy building, not changing the default.

tsrs_api handlers are private; tsrs_api::checker::dispatch::handle is pub and takes/returns tsrs JSON values (not text), so a custom CheckerHost could skip the text step. Going fully direct on tsrs_checker::Checker *_exported APIs is feasible but ~1.5-3 weeks, unstable across pins, and all-or-nothing per snapshot.

Code smells noted: string-keyed identity maps ("path:name"), starts_with scans in types/global.rs, name-pattern classification in types/ambient.rs, 36 bool fields in core structs, 215 `_ =>` arms with no clippy lint enforcing the no-wildcard rule.
Default collapseInheritedProps is already 'dependencies' at packages/storybook/src/provider.ts:47, with changesets in place; Chakra Button drops from 1,141 to ~21 rows.

code.finding: Addon default collapseInheritedProps is 'dependencies' on main.
Probe diagnostics call (getSemanticDiagnostics) used to find failing generic instantiations; ~800 ms, the single largest handler cost on shadcn.
Converter::fields batches isReadonlySymbol for every property plus types_of_symbols; source of Chakra's 743k sub-requests and most of its 261 MB batch bytes.
Converter::parts (members_text/type_arguments_text) issues per-item getTypesOfType/getTypeArguments loops that could use rpc.batch.

workflow: Verify a benchmark comparison is valid before trusting it: the old binary exited instantly because it rejected flags, producing a bogus 0.00 s result.
Use CPU time and interleaved runs when the machine is loaded (load 11-30 here); wall time is unreliable.
`python3 -I` drops the script directory from sys.path, so it breaks scripts like weekly.py that import sibling modules; use it only for standalone scripts.
An automated bisect must toggle each flag independently; the first bisect named the wrong commit because the script tied dependency loading to --no-checker.
`sample` needs `-wait` to attach at process launch for short runs; aggregate samples across threads and exclude idle waits (kevent, semaphore_wait_trap).
Quoting a fast-mode number beside quality-mode results is misleading; state the mode with each speed figure.
Clean multi-GB build directories and bisect worktrees after profiling; keep only needed binaries.
Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user instructions; claims should be checked against code before presenting.

friction: The first weekly run crashed at startup because of `python3 -I`, and the exit code 0 came only from the trailing echo, so the failure was initially masked.
The Chakra oracle hit its 3600 s timeout on a loaded machine (load ~11-30 from other sessions), leaving no accuracy number for Chakra and noisy timings everywhere.
The first bisect produced a wrong culprit commit because of a script flag-coupling bug and had to be redone.
The October binary rejected newer flags, which made the first old-vs-new comparison invalid and cost several debugging steps.
`sample` attached too late on the first profiling attempt.

The user was understandably frustrated that the 15x claim no longer held, that HTML attributes appeared to be un-walked-back, and that the checker was called through JSON; the speed scorecard that would have caught the regression had been removed after failing on noisy runners.
Handoff files live in /tmp/claude-501, which does not survive a restart.
Worker cap of three means the Level 1 JSON-parse-once change is held back until the prototype reports.

Diagnose why 62.9% of Mantine (and 24.5% of Chakra) props are 'not judged'; decide whether the 50% coverage floor stays.

Await the Level 2 no-JSON-text prototype and the request-reduction worker (isReadonlySymbol, per-run memo of repeated requests); then Level 1 parse-once in rpc.rs (~310 ms on shadcn).
Investigate the ~800 ms getSemanticDiagnostics probe call and the unexplained ~250 ms before first component answers.
